A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fragment temperature is a measure of the temperature at which the fragments are emitted.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the fragment kinetic energies are a good thermometer, but they are not a thermometer that is sensitive to the initial state of the reaction.
the temperature obtained from the fragment kinetic energy spectra is not necessarily a good indicator of the temperature of the source.

the fragment kinetic energy spectra are not directly related to the excitation energy of the system, but are rather a result of the competition between two processes: (a) the decay of the excited system by emission of fragments, and (b) the decay by emission of light particles (mainly neutrons) which are not observed in the fragment kinetic energy spectrum.
